title: Inertia is the tendency to resist a change in motion
summary: NASA Glenn names inertia as the tendency of an object to resist changes in whether it is resting or moving.
body: On the same laws page, NASA Glenn says every object remains at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless an outside force compels a change. It then names that tendency: inertia is resistance to a change in the state of motion. The examples on the page are an airplane when the throttle moves, a ball coming down through the air, a model rocket leaving the pad, and a kite when the wind shifts. Page last updated 27 June 2024.

sources.title: Newton's Laws of Motion
sources.author: Nancy Hall, NASA Glenn Research Center
sources.note: Public-domain NASA Glenn page, last updated 27 June 2024. Paraphrase of the sentence that defines inertia as resistance to a change in the state of motion.
